moduleTitle: Evaluating application data with Insights for Business Architects
learningObjectives: Describe the benefits of using Insights in data analysis.
Explain the role of BIX in data analysis for a Pega application.
Create a table and chart Insight.

elements.description: Explore Data is the Constellation View-based landing page for querying, filtering, sorting and grouping authorized application data. Save a useful query as an Insight; it is not limited to an authoring-only App Studio screen.
An Insight saves a query rule and its table/chart presentation for reuse or sharing. Sharing the definition does not guarantee identical data for every viewer or grant new authorization.
Insights provide self-service, low-code data analysis:
items: Business users can answer operational questions
Share results — without writing code or exporting to another tool

elements.text: An Insight is a saved 'lens' on your data: point it at your Cases and it renders the answer as a clear table or chart you can pin up and share, instead of digging through raw records each time.

bulletPoints: Explore Data supports application-user analysis and Insight creation, not only App Studio authors.
An Insight = a data query rendered as a table or chart, shareable between users.
Insights support data-driven decisions by surfacing team/process performance.

elements.description: Presents query results as rows and columns — ideal for detailed, record-level review (e.g., a list of Assistance Request Cases created in the last 30 days with key fields).
Presents query results as a visualization (e.g., bar, line, or pie chart) — ideal for spotting trends, comparisons, and distributions at a glance (e.g., Cases per day, by status, or by region).

elements.text: A table supports row/column review. A line chart suits daily trends; a pie chart suits part-to-whole proportions rather than every time series.

bulletPoints: Use a table Insight for detailed, row-level data; use a chart Insight to visualize trends/comparisons.
Both are created from the same underlying data query and can be shared.
Add/remove fields in Columns for tables or Measures/Dimensions for charts. Measures alone enables Simple Value summaries; choose an appropriate display/layout, then save the Insight.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: The Role of BIX in Data Analysis

elements.description: BIX extracts Pega transactional data in batches, one class at a time, for downstream analytics. It supplies the extract part of ETL and supports full/incremental extraction; it does not by itself transform/load or analyze the external warehouse.

items: INSIGHTS — analyze and visualize data IN Pega (in-platform, self-service)
BIX — EXTRACTS data to external systems for analysis OUTSIDE Pega (use when combining with external BI tools)

elements.text: Insights is reading the data where it lives (in Pega); BIX is the delivery truck that ships copies of the data to an external warehouse (a data warehouse/BI tool) for heavy-duty analysis.

bulletPoints: Insights = in-platform analysis/visualization; BIX = extract data to external systems for external BI/reporting.
Use configured extraction plus downstream import/analysis for cross-system or historical questions; external analysis is not accomplished by extraction alone.

examPitfalls.title: Insights vs. BIX
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The key distinction: Insights analyze/visualize data INSIDE Pega; BIX EXTRACTS data to external systems for analysis outside Pega.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: In-app, self-service charts/tables → Insights. Export data to an external BI/reporting tool → BIX.

examPitfalls.title: Table vs. chart Insight
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Choose by purpose: tables for detailed rows, charts for trends/comparisons.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Row-level detail → table Insight; visual trend/comparison → chart Insight.

examPitfalls.title: Where you build Insights
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Insights are built from the Explore Data landing page in App Studio (low-code), not from Dev Studio coding.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use Explore Data in the application to query/build Insights; it is not an App-Studio-only authoring screen.

examPitfalls.title: Insights are shareable
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A defining benefit is that Insights can be shared between users to align stakeholders.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Share the saved definition without assuming identical results or bypassing permissions.

examPitfalls.title: Insights are self-service/low-code
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Insights enable business users to analyze data without code or exporting to another tool.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: If a question stresses no-code, in-platform analysis, the answer is Insights (not BIX).

practiceQuiz.scenario: An application user wants Explore Data to turn a query into a reusable chart. Which capability is this?

options.text: Insights (from the Explore Data landing page)
BIX extract to an external database

practiceQuiz.hint: Insights are in-platform, low-code, shareable visualizations built from saved data queries.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Explore Data supports creating and saving Insights within the application; BIX is external extraction rather than in-app visualization.

optionExplanations.B: External extraction adds an unnecessary step.
optionExplanations.C: Mapping data does not build charts.
optionExplanations.D: Permissions do not visualize query results.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An enterprise must combine Pega Case data with data from other systems in an external data warehouse and BI tool. Which capability fits?

options.text: BIX (Business Intelligence Exchange) to extract data out of Pega

practiceQuiz.hint: BIX is used when data analysis happens OUTSIDE Pega, in an external BI tool or data warehouse.
practiceQuiz.rationale: BIX (Business Intelligence Exchange) extracts Pega application data to external databases or flat files for analysis in external BI tools. Insights and the Explore Data page analyze data inside Pega Platform without extraction.

optionExplanations.A: BIX supplies data for external analysis.
optionExplanations.B: An in-app chart is not extraction.
optionExplanations.C: A table alone does not export the warehouse data.
optionExplanations.D: Explore Data is the in-app analysis workspace.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A manager needs a quick visual of how many Assistance Request Cases were created per day over the last month to spot a trend. Which Insight type is best?
practiceQuiz.hint: A chart Insight renders trends visually — making patterns and changes easy to spot at a glance.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A time-series chart, such as a line chart, supports daily trends. A pie chart shows proportions and is not interchangeable for every time trend; the table gives detailed rows.

optionExplanations.B: Rows make trends harder to compare.
optionExplanations.C: Extraction alone provides no trend visualization.
optionExplanations.D: Conditional decisions do not plot historical counts.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An auditor needs a detailed, row-level list of specific Cases with several fields for review. Which Insight type is most appropriate?
practiceQuiz.hint: A table Insight shows row-by-row detail for in-depth record-level review and analysis.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A table Insight presents detailed rows and columns ideal for record-level review and drill-down analysis. Charts show aggregated patterns; BIX exports data to external systems; SLAs govern assignment timing.

optionExplanations.A: Rows and columns fit case-level auditing.
optionExplanations.B: An aggregate pie hides individual records.
optionExplanations.C: External extraction is not necessary here.
optionExplanations.D: Deadlines do not produce case listings.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A business stakeholder asks a BA to explain the difference between Pega Insights and the Business Intelligence Exchange (BIX) feature. Which statement best contrasts the two?

options.text: Insights analyze/visualize data inside Pega; BIX extracts data to external systems for analysis outside Pega
Insights extract data externally; BIX visualizes inside Pega
Both require Dev Studio coding only

practiceQuiz.hint: Insights are for in-platform analysis; BIX is the tool for extracting data OUT of Pega.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Insights provide in-platform analysis and visualization without leaving Pega. BIX extracts data to external systems for off-platform BI reporting. Their roles are complementary, not reversed or identical.

optionExplanations.A: The distinction is in-app analysis versus extraction.
optionExplanations.C: Extraction and visualization are different operations.
optionExplanations.D: Self-service Insights contradicts the coding-only claim.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which landing page lets application users query data and build Insights?
practiceQuiz.hint: The Explore Data landing page's name directly describes its purpose — exploring and querying application data.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Explore Data supports query/filter/group and Insight creation in the application; it is not restricted to App Studio authoring.

optionExplanations.B: Records maintenance is not the analysis workspace.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is recommending Insights to a business analyst who currently exports data to spreadsheets for analysis. Which TWO are key benefits of using Pega Insights for data analysis?

options.text: Business users get self-service, low-code analysis without exporting data
Results can be shared between users to align stakeholders
They replace the need for authentication

practiceQuiz.hint: Authorized users can reuse query presentations; data access remains governed separately.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Insights offer self-service, low-code analysis with shareable results so business users can build and share reports independently. They do not delete Cases or replace security controls. No partial credit.

optionExplanations.A: In-app exploration avoids manual spreadsheet exports.
optionExplanations.B: Sharing helps stakeholders discuss common results.
optionExplanations.C: Queries do not delete their source cases.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team wants the SAME analysis visible to multiple stakeholders rather than each rebuilding it. What feature of Insights helps?

options.text: Insights can be saved and shared between users
Insights can only be viewed by their creator
Insights must be re-created per user
Insights require BIX to be viewed

practiceQuiz.hint: Share a saved query/presentation definition, while retaining each viewer’s access controls.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Saving and sharing avoids rebuilding the query presentation. Different viewers may see different authorized data or different results after data changes; sharing is not an identical frozen snapshot.

optionExplanations.A: Saved sharing avoids rebuilding the analysis.
optionExplanations.C: A saved Insight can be reused.
optionExplanations.D: BIX is not required for in-app viewing.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is presenting the value of the Insights feature to an operations manager during a product demo. Why do organizations use Insights to evaluate application data?

options.text: To analyze operations and understand team and process performance for better decisions

practiceQuiz.hint: Insights help organizations analyze operational performance and understand team and process metrics.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Insights expose operational measures for analysis. Authentication verifies identity, Access Roles govern permissions, and routing allocates work; those are different purposes.

optionExplanations.B: Identity verification is a security task.
optionExplanations.C: Permission configuration is not operational analysis.
optionExplanations.D: Assignment routing does not evaluate performance.

quickRecap.value: Constellation application landing page for querying and analyzing authorized data.
A saved data query rendered as a table or chart/visualization; shareable between users; low-code.
Table = detailed rows; chart = visual trends/comparisons. Same query, different rendering.
Batch extraction, one class at a time; full/incremental modes. Downstream transform/load/analysis remains separate.
Insights = analyze IN Pega (self-service). BIX = extract OUT of Pega for external/large-scale analytics.
